public_rationale: The evidence challenges parts of the claim but does not support a clean verdict under the required financial matching rules. CoreWeave's reported 2024 net loss was $863 million, below billions on an annual net-loss reading. CNBC reported an approximately $5 billion OpenAI loss for that year, consistent with that component. Midjourney's founder had publicly described his company as profitable, but the verified statement concerns 2022. The claim names neither an accounting basis nor a loss period. With its accounting basis unknown, these differently defined figures cannot establish a supported, contradicted or mixed financial verdict.
limitations: This is not a finding that NVIDIA was the only profitable provider.
The annual net-loss reading would count CoreWeave's figure against the claim; a cash-burn reading requires different evidence.
Private-company reporting does not consistently define profit or losses.
Some original sources could not be read, and no inaccessible or partial page is cited as evidence.

statement.excerpt: It's also important to note that absolutely nobody other than NVIDIA is making any money from generative AI. CoreWeave loses billions of dollars, OpenAI loses billions of dollars, Anthropic loses billions of dollars, and I can't find a single company providing generative AI-powered software that's making a profit.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

from_speaker: making any money from generative AI
a single company providing generative AI-powered software that's making a profit
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of making money here is earning profit after expenses, because the following sentences explicitly discuss losses and profitability.
The NVIDIA exception defines the scope; it is not a conditional antecedent.
I assess 2024, the latest completed annual period before the post. Annual results are the ordinary comparison for the named companies' losses; the speaker supplies no period.
I read billions as at least $2 billion for each named company individually, rather than their combined losses.
A profitable diversified company is not automatically a counterexample: its profit must be attributable to generative AI.
The quoted passage specifies no common accounting basis. I therefore retain unknown rather than selecting GAAP, adjusted earnings, or cash burn to produce a verdict.
The statement about what the speaker could find is treated as part of the surrounding factual assertion, not as a separately testable account of his search.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable 2024 evidence establishes that NVIDIA earned profit from generative AI, no other provider did, and CoreWeave, OpenAI and Anthropic each lost at least $2 billion on the specified accounting basis. Missing disclosures alone cannot establish the universal negative.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable 2024 evidence identifies a non-NVIDIA provider earning profit attributable to generative AI, or establishes that a named company's loss was below $2 billion. A scoring verdict requires resolving the unspecified accounting basis.
